answer: The matrix representations most often highlighted are the graph adjacency matrix, the graph Laplacian (and its normalized variants), and related similarity/co-occurrence matrices such as random-walk or diffusion matrices. In unsupervised feature learning, these methods are commonly interpreted as linear-algebraic matrix factorization or low-rank approximation problems: the learned node embeddings are viewed as factors that approximately reconstruct the chosen graph matrix, or equivalently as coordinates in a spectral subspace given by eigenvectors/singular vectors of that matrix.
confidence_reasoning: This is a standard and widely cited interpretation of unsupervised graph embedding methods, though exact emphasis can vary by source and method.
